I spent around fifteen years as a historian and researcher, mostly in and about
Afghanistan, before moving into software in 2021. Since then I've been an ML
engineer at ZenML, working on [ZenML](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml) and
[Kitaru](https://kitaru.ai). I live in Delft, in the Netherlands, with two cats.

Most of my historical work came down to reading large piles of messy,
contradictory sources, deciding which ones to trust, and turning them into
something structured enough to reason about. That turns out to be most of the
work of evaluating and training agents. Reading an agent's trace is source
criticism: its account of what it did is
[testimony, not fact](/posts/2026-10-13-agent-swarm-observability-tools.html).
Building an eval or an
[RL environment](/posts/2026-06-20-my-first-rl-environment.html) means turning
a messy record into a task you can check, which is what I did with ISAF press
releases on the way to
[finetuned models that beat GPT-4](/posts/2024-07-01-full-finetuned-model-evaluation.html).
I'm always happy to talk about evals, RL environments or agent observability;
the easiest way to reach me is on [LinkedIn](https://linkedin.com/in/strickvl)
or [Twitter](https://twitter.com/strickvl).

This site has two halves. The [technical](/technical.html) side is where I work
things out in public: these days that's mostly agents, reinforcement learning
for agents, and evals. The [personal](/personal.html) side goes back to 2010
and covers Afghanistan, language learning, maths, learning how to learn, and
the books I've been reading. If you're not sure where to start, the
[series](/series.html) collect longer runs of posts about a single project,
course or book. Each half has its own RSS feed
([technical](/technical.xml), [personal](/personal.xml)).

The two halves meet more often than you might expect. Some of the tools below
are for historians and researchers, and I publish datasets on
[Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/strickvl), including ISAF press releases
from Afghanistan and records from the Guantánamo military commissions.

## Books

- [*DeepSeek in Practice*](https://www.packtpub.com/en-us/product/deepseek-in-practice-9781806020850)
  (Packt, 2025), with Andy Peng and Duarte O. Carmo
- [*The Taliban Reader*](https://hurstpublishers.com/book/the-taliban-reader/)
  (2018), edited with Felix Kuehn
- [*An Enemy We Created: The Myth of the Taliban-Al Qaeda Merger in Afghanistan*](https://hurstpublishers.com/book/an-enemy-we-created/)
  (2012), with Felix Kuehn
- [*Poetry of the Taliban*](https://hurstpublishers.com/book/poetry-of-the-taliban/)
  (2012), edited with Felix Kuehn
- [*My Life with the Taliban*](https://hurstpublishers.com/book/my-life-with-the-taliban/)
  (2010), Abdul Salam Zaeef's memoir, edited with Felix Kuehn
- [*Master Arabic*](https://incrementalelephant.gumroad.com/l/masterarabic-basic)
  (2017), a guide for intermediate Arabic students

Felix and I also run [First Draft Publishing](https://www.firstdraft-publishing.com),
a small publishing house for niche-interest books.

## Other things I've made

- The [LLMOps Database](https://www.zenml.io/llmops-database), which I curate:
  over 2,000 real-world case studies of LLMs in production
- [AIE Talks](https://aietalks.com), summaries and timestamps for every talk on
  the AI Engineer YouTube channel
- [MLOps Talks](https://mlopstalks.com), the same for the MLOps Community's
  talks, podcast episodes and meetups
- [hinbox](https://github.com/strickvl/hinbox), which pulls people, places and
  organisations out of historical documents
- [tinbox](https://github.com/strickvl/tinbox), a translator in a box
- [panlabel](https://github.com/strickvl/panlabel), a converter between data
  annotation formats
- [Sources & Methods](https://www.sourcesandmethods.com), a podcast I ran with
  Matt Trevithick about what people read and the tools they use to get their
  work done
- [Gemini by Example](https://www.geminibyexample.com), a reference for the
  Gemini API and SDK
- [Ekko](https://ekko-realtime.com), an open-source framework for adding
  realtime messaging to web applications
